body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Saturday, August 15, 2026, and we’re starting the day with a reminder of the Eagles’ resolve. Today’s top story follows Bakersfield Christian High School’s football team as they regroup after a state title loss. We’re looking at a high of 95° and a low of 69°, with clear skies and good air quality. Let’s see what happened overnight and what the day holds.

## The Kern Overnight

A night that opened with a road-rage pair stalling traffic on White Lane and closed with a stolen van on Kentucky Street and a fender dispute between big rigs at the Flying J. Law enforcement carried most of the load: a 90-plus mph DUI south of the Grapevine, a reported theft from a mobile home park on Barlow Road, and the night's most serious call — an attempt-to-locate after a woman was seen crying for help out the window of a red pickup at Chester and Belle Terrace. Fire crews were comparatively quiet: a residential alarm that amounted to nothing and a vehicle accident that drew an engine, battalion and rescue unit before the air went quiet.

Around 11:34 p.m., Bakersfield police broadcast an attempt-to-locate and welfare check after a caller described an older-model red truck at South Chester Avenue and Belle Terrace — a male hanging out the driver's window, a female crying and saying she needed help. The truck was last seen traveling southbound. It's the kind of call dispatchers don't sit on: no description of plates or direction of travel beyond southbound, so the broadcast went out citywide for any unit to catch the truck. No further update was heard on the air before the feed moved on.

Just after 9:23 p.m., city units were sent to White Lane for a possible road-rage disturbance: a blue Honda with paper plates and a white pickup, both eastbound, repeatedly stopping and blocking the roadway. Dispatched as a 415 vehicle with no further update heard.

At 10:33 p.m., a white 2001 Dodge van with California plates was reported stolen on Kentucky Street. Officers took the report; no arrests were announced on the air.

About 11:39 p.m., CHP broadcast a 23152 on southbound I-5 south of the Grapevine — a newer black pickup at speeds over 90, passing on the shoulder, the driver seen drinking from an open container. Units were responding as the feed moved on.

Shortly before 3 a.m., a traffic collision in the Flying J truck stop parking lot at Frazier Park: the victim's burgundy Freightliner was hit by a red Peterbilt, with the other party denying involvement. CHP was investigating the hit-and-run claim.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 95° and a low around 69° tonight. It's currently 66° at Meadows Field (KBFL). No active weather alerts for Kern County. Air quality is 39 — good.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that** Bakersfield Christian High School’s football team is regrouping after a tough state title loss. The Eagles are determined to right the wrongs of the past and come back stronger this season. This story of resilience and resolve is a reminder that setbacks can fuel future success.

**According to 23ABC,** Kern County supervisors are exploring a proposal that would place Kern and dozens of other counties in a new state, separate from coastal California. Kern County District 3 Supervisor Jeff Flores said the effort is about making sure the region's industries and way of life are taken seriously by state leaders. An analysis presented to the board found the proposed inland state would account for only about 15 percent of California's current real GDP. CSU Bakersfield economics professor Richard Gearhart said that number tells a stark story about what separation would actually mean for the region.

**KGET 17 tells us that** Kern County officials will inform the public on local ICE activity during a community forum on August 25. The meeting will provide residents with information and an opportunity to ask questions about immigration enforcement in our area.

**23ABC shares that** Carlos Baldovinos, executive director of the Mission at Kern County, traveled to San Diego on August 12 to celebrate the public release of a federal best practices toolkit aimed at addressing addiction treatment within the homeless community — a project he helped build from the ground up. The toolkit outlines best practices for working with individuals dealing with addiction within the homeless population, covering topics including program length, transitional housing, long-term mentorship, and workforce development.

**23ABC also reports that** Bakersfield's police and fire chiefs presented their Fourth of July reports during a Friday meeting, revealing both progress and ongoing concerns about fireworks-related incidents in the city. Kevin Albertson, Chief of the Bakersfield Fire Department, said the holiday brought serious consequences for people across the state. A total of 106 citations were issued by the Bakersfield Police and Fire departments combined in relation to the holiday. Compared to 2025, fire-related responses to both departments dropped 6% in 2026. Despite the decrease, residents and officials say more work remains.

## Something good

Bakersfield and Tehachapi airports will receive a portion of $109 million in federal aviation funding. This financial support will enhance local airport infrastructure and services. It’s a welcome boost for our community’s transportation network.

## Coming up this week

Here’s what’s on the calendar for the week ahead:

On Tuesday, August 18, the Multi Modal Transportation And Traffic Safety Committee meets at 12:00 p.m. The Historic Preservation Commission also convenes at 4:00 p.m. Later that afternoon, the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission gathers at 2:00 p.m.

Wednesday, August 19 brings the Water Board meeting at 10:00 a.m.

Thursday, August 20 features the Planning Commission meeting at 5:30 p.m.

And for entertainment, the Fox Theater has a full lineup: Los Yonic's Zamacona, Los caminantes, y Grupo Yndio take the stage on August 22. Rodney Carrington performs on August 27. CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE follows on August 28. Willie Barcena and Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix both perform on August 29. Finally, MI HISTORIA TOUR LEYENDAS DEL MARIACHI USA comes to town on September 4.
